children: New Delhi, Nov. 15 -- Lalit Modi, the founder and former Commissioner of the Indian Premier League (IPL) has announced that he has acquired British citizenship. Lalit Modi, who left India in May 2010 after the conclusion of the third season of the IPL amid financial irregularities and money laundering, made the announcement on Saturday.

"A PROUD MOMENT. A NEW CHAPTER. Today, 14 November 2026, I had the honour of addressing the Oxford Union, where I publicly shared a very special and personal milestone. I AM PROUD TO BE A BRITISH CITIZEN," Lalit Modi said.
The 62-year-old, who had been living in London since his departure from India, said the UK had been his home for many years.
"The United Kingdom has been my home for many years. It is a country I have come to admire and appreciate deeply - its people, institutions, traditions and values," he said.

He thanked his family, friends and the Oxford Union for being part of the memorable occasion. Modi also noted that sharing the announcement on the occasion of King Charles III's birthday made the moment particularly special.
" A new chapter, with much to look forward to. And on His Majesty King Charles III's birthday, a particularly special day to share this moment. God Save the King," he said.

Born in Delhi as the son of industrialist KK Modi and the grandson of Gujar Mal Modi, the founder of Modi Group, Lalit Modi began his career at the family-controlled International Tobacco Company Limited.

He, however, is best known for his role as a Cricket administrator, which began with the Rajasthan Cricket Association in 2005. Three years later, in 2008, he played a key role in the founding of IPL, which was set up by the BCCI to challenge the rebel Indian Cricket League (ICL).

While the IPL was a runaway success, Lalit Modi ran into trouble with the BCCI in 2010 over the newly allotted franchise based in Kochi, Kerala, in which the then MoS External Affairs, Shashi Tharoor's wife, Sunanda Pushkar, was given sweat equity.

Amid growing friction and investigation into his financial dealings, Lalit Modi left India and has been living in London ever since. Though he has been facing multiple investigations in India, Lalit Modi has disputed the 'fugitive' tag on him.

You can apply for British citizenship through naturalization if you are 18 or older, have lived lawfully in the UK for the required number of years, hold Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) or settled status, and pass mandatory knowledge and character checks.
Those applying for British citizenship should have lived in the UK for at least 5 years, with no more than 450 days outside the UK over the 5 years, and no more than 90 days in the final 12 months.
Spouses or partners of British citizens are also eligible to apply for citizenship after they have lived in the UK for at least 3 years.

Those who are for British citizenship include those who do not hold ILR, settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or Indefinite Leave to Enter. If you do not met the 3-year or 5-year continuous residence rules, or have exceeded the maximum permitted absence days or have a if you have a criminal or breach record, you are not eligible to apply.
